plan: In this sealed-bid/ascending-clock hybrid, the mechanism functions like a second-price auction: I pay the second-highest bid if I win. Bidding my true value ($21) is a dominant strategy—bidding higher risks paying more than the prize is worth, while bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. Since values are independently drawn and I have no information about other bidders' values in this single round, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit.

Since this is effectively a second-price auction mechanism (the ascending clock ensures I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid), the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Bidding exactly $22 ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the highest competing bid, and I'll pay the second-highest bid price, maximizing expected profit without risk of overpaying or losing value from underbidding.

Bidding truthfully ensures I win whenever my value exceeds others' bids and pay only the second-highest bid, maximizing expected profit. There's no incentive to shade my bid up or down given the mechanics described.
